initialize crew lifescores for shift.#comment: Crew emergency decisions. CREW_DIVERT: the mission is cancelled and the helicopter goes to the hospital (a death forces it, a critical member lets the user choose Divert or Continue). The limits are the LifeScore up to which a crew member aboard at the base finds the police car (CREW_POLICE_LIMIT) and the ambulance (CREW_AMBULANCE_LIMIT).

Crew emergency with the crew outside (user rules of 2026-10-18): CREW_OPS_ABORT yes stops the visits of the ground operations (the doctor goes back, the patient stays for another unit), CREW_NO_PATIENT yes = the helicopter will not carry a patient, CREW_TOUR_ACTIVE 1 while a crew tour runs, CRIT_FAIL_ACTIVE yes after a critical failure (mayday).

Hospital unload of the crew in parallel with the patient (crew hospital scene stretchers): CHS_PARALLEL yes while the casualties are extracted during the patient unloading, CHS_MEDIC_HURT / CHS_PAPER_HURT yes when the member who would hand over the patient / do the paperwork is a casualty and stays in the seat, CHS_AMB_TURN the casualty whose turn it is to use the ambulance.

CREW_HOSPITAL_n 1: the member was unloaded at the hospital (the stretcher arrived at hospital_door or at the hospital with the ambulance). The dispatch page shows it in red in place of the critical or deceased row.
Locals survive reload_mission: the failure of the previous mission must not label the new one (end menu text) and is cleared at every mission start.

start crew lifescore monitor.#comment: A second start in the same mission pass would double every impact (two monitors apply the damage twice), so it is refused and traced. L:CREW_MONITOR_STARTS counts the starts for the whole flight.

do.#comment: Crew health simulation off: nothing to measure, the monitor waits (settings page, Crew health simulation).
Crew health simulation off: nothing to measure, the monitor waits (settings page, Crew health simulation).
Crew health simulation off: nothing to measure, the monitor waits (settings page, Crew health simulation).

post crew safety message.#comment: Short crew status: the role instead of the member number and no score. The status always ends with a period. It is a report of the crew to the dispatcher (sender -OUT-); the on-screen message is for the user.

set_message.text: CREW: {0} {1} Cause: {2}

then.#comment: A hoist operator who died on the hook and did not fall (CREW_FATAL_ON_HOOK yes, set by hoist cable operator lost) is brought aboard with the cable: no dead asset on the ground.
A hoist operator who died on the hook and did not fall (CREW_FATAL_ON_HOOK yes, set by hoist cable operator lost) is brought aboard with the cable: no dead asset on the ground.

crew emergency destination menu.#comment: Hospital selection of the crew emergency, same choices as the destination menu of the patients: the user confirms the proposed hospital (hospital_user) or selects another one (map/list or custom DB, both end back here through user destination menu). The route to care continues only when CREW_DEST_CONFIRMED is yes.

set_message.text: Do you confirm location {1} (distance {0}Km) as hospital destination?
No hospital found. Select the hospital destination manually.

set_modal.title: CHOOSE DESTINATION
set_modal.text: Crew emergency: select the hospital for the injured crew

set_message.text: No destination selected, first select a destination, and then confirm

crew ops outside.#comment: 1 when a crew member is outside the helicopter (ground operations: hoist_crew, pax1, pax2 or pax3 exist) and no patient is aboard (L:HOISTED not 1).

sleep unless crew abort.#comment: Sleeps param seconds, one second at a time, and stops at once when the ground operations are aborted by a crew emergency (CREW_OPS_ABORT yes): the visit of the doctor does not go on for its whole time.

then.#comment: Skid or hoist operation aborted: the crew comes back with the pickup of the operation (the doctor, the patient stays), the program waits for it.

crew emergency route to care.#comment: The hospital of the dispatch (hospital_user, the one chosen for the patients or by the user) is also the proposed hospital of the crew emergency; it is queried, with the same macro of the patient flow, only when the dispatch has none yet. Without a result the user selects it from the menu.

With a patient aboard (L:HOISTED 1, not delivered yet) the normal destination flow runs from the confirmed hospital: route, unloading, ambulance button and FORCE_AMBULANCE as for any patient; its end (Return to base or continue menu) hands over the critical crew and sets the return to base. Without a patient the crew flow runs alone.

crew emergency response.#comment: First event: a death diverts the mission at once, a critical member (LifeScore 10 or less) lets the user choose between Divert and Continue. After Continue only a death diverts. Nothing happens when the mission is already diverted (CREW_DIVERT yes).

else.#comment: With a patient aboard (L:HOISTED 1, not delivered yet) the helicopter goes to a hospital whatever the answer, and a critical member is handed over there anyway: no question, the mission simply continues. The question is asked before the patient is aboard (Divert cancels the mission) and after the delivery (Divert to a hospital or go on to the base).
Crew outside, no patient aboard (ground operations): the abort is mandatory, no Divert or Continue question (user, 2026-10-18).

crew presence flags.#comment: Presence per person aboard. Pilot from L:IMPL_PILOT0 (0 = present). Copilot, medic and the rear crew come from the seat tracker, which follows every person between seats. SDK_CABIN_PAX_5: 0 no stretcher, 1 empty stretcher, 2 stretcher with patient.

monitor aircraft crash impact.#comment: Starts the impact model: initial state, velocity history and the loop. There is deliberately no watchdog that restarts the loop: a stalled thread must be explained, not hidden (the 169.12 stall is still under investigation). Stages are traced so that the last row shows where a thread stops.

Performance options (settings page, PERFORMANCE): PERF_SAMPLING picks the tick (fast 0.02 s, balanced 0.05 s, light 0.1 s) and PERF_ALTITUDE_GATE lets the loop sleep above 450 ft above ground until 400 ft (or the ground). cm_cfg makes the first tick read them; they are read again every 50 ticks.

crash monitor loop.#comment: One thread for the whole impact model, so there is no lock to leave stuck and no state shared between paths. Every tick (0.02 s) it reads the acceleration and the world velocity. Minor injuries: acceleration resultant of 80 ft/s2 (about 2.5 g), 0 to 3 (not below 70), plus 3 to 8 (not below 40) from 120 ft/s2; it rearms below 60. Crash tiers (rearm below 64): 150 ft/s2 or 25 ft/s lost gives 7 to 20 (not below 20); the loss of world velocity within about 0.2 s then gives 10 to 30 at 50 ft/s, 10 to 30 with failures and fires at 90 ft/s and 45 to 60 at 150 ft/s (ignores the member lock). The crash path has two more triggers that do not depend on catching an acceleration spike (a single-frame spike can fall between two ticks): a new simulator touchdown speed (PLANE TOUCHDOWN NORMAL VELOCITY changes and its square reaches 625) and a loss of 25 ft/s of world velocity within one tick below 100 ft above ground; either one grades the impact with the same squared-velocity table. Above 150 ft/s the crash is fatal for everyone aboard (score 100, ignores the member lock). While slew mode is active (IS SLEW ACTIVE, which also covers the repositioning done by the mission itself) and for 15 ticks after it, every trigger is suppressed, so a teleport is never taken for an impact; the height guard and the unchanged velocity during a pause are secondary. The damage chain is long, and the 169.16 test showed a RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded) at the catastrophic tier, after the three previous tiers had run in the same pass without a sleep: the stack of a thread only unwinds at a sleep, so every damage application (and every member inside it) is followed by a short sleep, and the catch starts with one so that its own trace cannot overflow. An error in a tick is caught and traced, and the loop goes on. Every impact traces probe_trigger and probe_after (L:CRASH, the simulator touchdown velocity, on-ground, height, vertical speed, ground speed, world vertical velocity before and now) to compare the signals in a test; a probe error is caught on its own and cannot stop the injuries. Escalation: a heavier impact inside a chain of bounces, while the crash path is not rearmed yet, is graded too and applies only the tiers above the heaviest one already applied since the last rearm (cm_chain_tier): the 169.25 test showed an impact of about 120 ft/s lost swallowed 0.04 s after one of about 26 ft/s.

then.#comment: Crew health simulation off: the impact model has no crew to hurt, so the loop waits until the option is on again and then re-seeds its velocity history. Applied at the next option read, at most 50 ticks after the option is turned off.

try.#comment: Escalation: a heavier impact inside a chain of bounces (the crash path is not rearmed yet) must not be swallowed. The same two triggers open the window while the crash path is disarmed and the heaviest tier of the chain is below the catastrophic one (cm_chain_tier); the window then applies only the tiers above the chain tier.

then.#comment: A spike of acceleration alone is not an impact: a soft touchdown or a hoist jolt gives 120 to 170 ft/s2 for a frame with almost no change of velocity (169.20 test: 144 and 174 ft/s2 with 2 and 6 ft/s lost at 0.5 to 2.6 ft/s of descent). Without the touchdown or velocity trigger, the acceleration triggers count only when the velocity changed by at least 10 ft/s (dv2 100) in the window; otherwise the event is traced as ignored and both paths wait to be rearmed.
Disarmed (the impact belongs to a chain of bounces already graded): only the tiers above the heaviest one applied since the last rearm count, never the same or a lighter tier again.

set_message.text: Impact detected. Crew shaken but conscious.
Severe impact detected. Crew injuries reported.
Heavy impact detected. Serious crew injuries likely.
Catastrophic impact detected. Crew casualties likely.

try.#comment: Altitude gate: above 450 ft above ground, with both paths armed and no slew hold, for 20 ticks in a row the loop sleeps until the aircraft is below 400 ft or on the ground; the velocity history and the touchdown reading are then re-seeded so the first tick after the wake cannot be taken for an impact. A crash against a cliff or an obstacle higher than that is not seen while it sleeps: the option OFF keeps the loop always active.

crew seat tracker tick.#comment: Who sits where. Persons keep their identity while moving between seats. A seat vacated and a seat filled in the same tick is a move; with several candidates the cabin-right seat takes the rear crew member first. A person leaving without a filled seat is outside; a filled seat without a mover takes the outside person by seat affinity (FO 3, P3 2, P1 4, P2 5).

crew member event announce.#comment: Announces a critical condition or a death to the survivors: report of the crew to the dispatcher (RescueTrack, sender -OUT-) and on-screen message. The mission abort is not announced here: Divert or Continue is the pilot decision, the abort is reported by crew emergency divert. After the first death the dispatcher answers that the accident report is required.

set_message.text: CREW LOSS: {0} deceased. Mission aborted, fly to the hospital.
CREW LOSS: {0} deceased.

else.#comment: A critical member is only announced: Divert or Continue is the user's choice (crew emergency choice), so no text may say that the mission is aborted.

set_message.text: CREW CRITICAL: {0}.

critical failure check.#comment: Called at the end of apply aircraft failure with the code: the critical failures (5 and 6 engine fire, 18 and 19 transmission damage) call the mayday.

critical failure mayday.#comment: A critical failure (param code: 5 and 6 engine fire, 18 and 19 transmission damage; called by apply aircraft failure) obliges to stop the helicopter and to call a mayday (user rule of 2026-10-18), whatever the crew emergency was doing: the ground operations are aborted (CREW_OPS_ABORT), the crew emergency route to care is stopped (CREW_MISSION_TERMINATED), the dispatcher is told, the crew calls the mayday on the radio (voice mayday) and after the landing the operation is terminated with the report. Once per mission (CRIT_FAIL_ACTIVE).

set_message.text: MAYDAY: {0}. Land as soon as possible and shut down.

text.text: MAYDAY MAYDAY MAYDAY. {0}. Landing and shutting down, request assistance.

params.text: Copy MAYDAY. Emergency services are alerted to your position. Land and shut down.

set_message.text: MAYDAY: helicopter stopped. Shut down and evacuate.

wait_modal.title: MAYDAY - OPERATION TERMINATED
wait_modal.text: A critical failure obliged the crew to stop the helicopter. The operation is terminated.

then.#comment: Status 7 (unavailable for dispatch) only with automatic status reports (DISPATCHER_AUTO 0), through Update_raw from dispatchphase, which updates RescueTrack in the language of the active status table. Phases 5 and 6 are avoided: the NEW DISPATCH thread answers them with ready dispatch, which reopens the briefing page.

set_message.text: MISSION FAILED - ALL CREW DECEASED. Operation terminated.
MISSION FAILED - PILOT AND COPILOT INCAPACITATED. Operation terminated.
MISSION FAILED - PILOT AND COPILOT DECEASED. Operation terminated.

wait_modal.title: MISSION FAILED
wait_modal.text: All crew members are deceased. The operation is terminated.

wait_modal.title: MISSION FAILED
wait_modal.text: Pilot and copilot are incapacitated. The operation is terminated.

wait_modal.title: MISSION FAILED
wait_modal.text: Pilot and copilot are deceased. The operation is terminated.

crew impact events.#comment: Evaluates every member marked after an impact once, with the final scores of the batch: alerts, critical and death events, survivors, the abort and the mission termination.

Pilot and copilot (or the only pilot when there is no copilot) are not fit to fly when dead or critical: a single pilot with one trained technical crew member can land only while the second one is fit, so both unfit ends the mission as with two deaths.

crew casualty plan.#comment: Who is aboard and hurt. A member counts when it is aboard (crew presence flags) and not already handed over (CCS_DONE_n). Casualty: LifeScore at or below CREW_AMBULANCE_LIMIT (10: critical or dead), injured: at or below CREW_POLICE_LIMIT (20). CCS_LOAD_MEMBER is the worst casualty (lowest score, lowest index on a tie), CCS_CASUALTY_COUNT, CCS_DEAD_COUNT and CCS_INJURED_COUNT count them, CCS_WALK_MEMBER is the pilot (1) when alive and not loaded, otherwise the copilot (3), otherwise 0.

params.state: plan load={local:CCS_LOAD_MEMBER} casualties={local:CCS_CASUALTY_COUNT} injured={local:CCS_INJURED_COUNT} dead={local:CCS_DEAD_COUNT} walk={local:CCS_WALK_MEMBER}

crew casualty scene vehicles.#comment: Police car and policeman parked about 50 m from the pre-set landing point (ccs_site, created by the caller from hospital_user or RTB_location), and, only when a crew member aboard is a casualty (CCS_CASUALTY_COUNT), the ambulance 34 m from it with its medic at the left side and the stretcher behind it (bearing2 180 is the rear door side). ccs_vehicles_ready is no (reset at every mission start), working, then yes; every caller waits for yes.

deceased patient police scene.#comment: Deceased patient aboard at the destination: the police car and its policeman are parked 50 m from the pre-set landing point (ccs_site) like in the crew casualty scene; the ambulance, the medic and the stretcher are the ones of the normal destination scene. Idempotent per mission (ccs_police_ready, reset at every mission start).

deceased patient police guard.#comment: The policeman keeps clear of the helipad while the patient is unloaded (the stretchers free it) and, when the helicopter prepares to leave (a fuel prime pump ON, or NR above 5 when GNDOPS_ROTOR is 1, above 86 when it is 0), walks 12 m from the helicopter to the bearing 300 or 30 closest to him and faces the user.

crew casualty load member.#comment: Loads the worst casualty (CCS_LOAD_MEMBER) without walking: the stretcher is driven to a point 4 m from the helicopter at the casualty door (ccs_door, helicopter-relative; around the nose when the door is on the other side of the helicopter than the stretcher, never across it), the door opens, the seat is released (the person disappears from the cabin and appears on the stretcher: Medic Stretcher VAR 2 3 is the carried load), the stretcher returns to the rear of the ambulance and is removed there. Every step is a synchronous command.

set_message.text: Casualty loaded into the ambulance.

crew casualty pilot walk.#comment: The pilot (or the copilot when the pilot is not available) leaves the helicopter and walks to the policeman without crossing the helicopter: directly when the policeman is on the door side, otherwise around the nose. The policeman points at the person. The pilot door is opened by the user (the same message and gate as the deboarding), the copilot door is opened by the scene. The caller then shows the end menu.

set_message.text: Open the pilot door to complete deboarding.

crew casualty destination scene.#comment: Base scene after a crew emergency or with a hurt crew member aboard: police car and policeman (and, for a casualty aboard, ambulance, medic and stretcher) already parked about 50 m away; the policeman (and the medic) walk to the helicopter at the side closest to each of them, the worst casualty is carried to the ambulance on a stretcher, and with a single casualty or none the pilot (or the copilot) walks around the nose to the policeman, who points at them. Two or more casualties: one is loaded and the end menu follows. The end menu (SUBMIT REPORT, END SHIFT, RELOAD MISSION) is the only exit; after a crew emergency no dispatch can be loaded or accepted.

set_message.text: EMERGENCY SERVICES ON SITE. COMPLETE THE SHUT DOWN PROCEDURE.
Choose END SHIFT or RELOAD MISSION on the tablet.

crew emergency choice.#comment: A critical (alive) crew member: the user decides. Divert cancels the mission and goes to the hospital of the dispatch (hospital_user); Continue keeps the mission, the critical member is handed over at the next hospital stop (forced) or at the base. The dispatch page is hidden first (it covered the modal until it hid itself near the scene) and the question is only on screen: it is a decision of the pilot, not a message of the crew to the dispatcher (the crew report of the critical member was posted by crew member event announce).

set_message.text: CREW EMERGENCY: a crew member is critical. Choose to divert to a hospital or to continue the mission.

set_modal.title: CREW EMERGENCY
set_modal.text: A crew member is critical. Divert to a hospital now, or continue the mission? At a hospital stop the critical crew is handed over anyway.

params.status: critical, mission continues. Handover at the next hospital stop.

set_message.text: The mission continues. The critical crew member is handed over at the next hospital stop or at the base.

crew emergency replacement unit.#comment: Name of the unit the dispatcher tasks when the mission is cancelled: purely informative, the unit is not simulated.

crew emergency divert.#comment: The mission is cancelled: the helicopter goes to the hospital of the dispatch to hand over the critical crew (and the patient aboard, with the normal destination flow). The crew tells the dispatcher (sender -OUT-); with a patient not loaded yet, who stays on scene, the dispatcher answers that it tasks another unit (the unit is not simulated). Idempotent per mission.

params.text: Mission aborted, crew member unfit. Patient on scene needs another unit.

value.text: Copy. Mission cancelled. {0} tasked to the scene.

params.text: Mission aborted, crew member unfit. Diverting to hospital.

crew hospital ambulance call.#comment: The ambulance of the hospital destination, as in user destination scene predefined1: it is created 70 m from hospital_user, drives to the waiting point DAMBU and sets L:AMBULANCE 2. Synchronous (the callers run it in their own thread or wait for L:AMBULANCE 2).

crew emergency ambulance prime.#comment: Ambulance for the crew alone at the hospital, same rules as the patient: with FORCE_AMBULANCE no and a hospital (POI_TYPE 2) the user asks for it with the button Unload to ambulance, which appears when the destination is confirmed and disappears at 0.2 NM or when selected; otherwise the ambulance comes by itself. Called enroute, never at the landing.

crew hospital police watch.#comment: A dead crew member aboard is met by the police at the hospital, 50 m from the landing point, like a dead patient (deceased patient police scene). Started at the confirmation of the hospital, acts at 2 NM.

crew hospital arrival.#comment: Crew alone (no patient aboard): landing at the hospital, rotor stop, unloading of the critical crew, then the return to base. The patient flow does the same through Return to base or continue menu.

set_message.text: LAND AND SET ENGINES TO IDLE or STOP to start unload procedure

crew hospital crew back.#comment: The patient unloading sends the medic and the copilot out of their seats (CREW_OUT_n) and the destination flow ends right after their boarding trigger, before the seat tracker sees them aboard again. Waits, at most 30 s, until every member up to CREW_MEMBER_CAP who walked is back in a seat. A casualty handed over (CCS_DONE_n) left the seat on a stretcher and is not waited for. A casualty never walks in the patient flow (CHS_MEDIC_HURT, CHS_PAPER_HURT), so this wait concerns the members who are fit.

crew hospital handover roles.#comment: Who of the members that normally walk in the patient flow is a casualty (aboard, not handed over, LifeScore at or below CREW_AMBULANCE_LIMIT). The medic who hands over the patient (hoist_crew) is member 2 (member 5 with five crew), the member who does the paperwork is member 4 (the copilot, member 3, with three crew). A casualty stays in the seat: the destination flow skips its seat triggers (the hoist_crew actor of the medic then is hospital staff) and the paperwork is skipped. Needs crew casualty plan to have run.

crew hospital scene place.#comment: One empty stretcher per casualty, on the scene with the rules of the ground team of the patient: after ambumedic and ambustretcher (already at DMED and DSTR) point at hospital_user, the stretchers are placed beside them with bearing2 270 (left of the patient stretcher) and 90 (right of the medic), 3 m, the second pair 6 m, so that they are separated whatever the helicopter heading. They point at hospital_user too. No extra medic: the medic of the patient is enough, the stretchers are numbered like the casualties (chs_str_1..4).

crew hospital scene stretchers.#comment: Called by the patient destination flows (User destination1 and 2) once the rotor has stopped, before the ground team moves. With a crew emergency active and a hospital stop (cambuchoice not yes) the casualties are extracted in parallel with the patient: the roles of the casualties are set (crew hospital handover roles), the stretchers are placed (crew hospital scene place) and crew hospital unload runs in its own thread, so the casualties are on their stretchers while the patient is handed over; each stretcher leaves for the hospital door after the patient (L:SAVED 1). crew hospital finish waits for CHS_UNLOADED. Without casualties nothing changes (CHS_PARALLEL no, the roles stay with the crew).

crew hospital finish.#comment: End of the destination flow of a patient while a crew emergency is active (called by Return to base or continue menu at a hospital stop): the casualties are handed over, then the helicopter returns to base. A critical member is handed over even when the user chose Continue. When the casualties were extracted in parallel with the patient (CHS_PARALLEL yes, crew hospital scene stretchers) this only waits for the end of that unload; otherwise (no casualty at the landing, other destination flows) the unload runs here, after the patient.

crew emergency return to base.#comment: After the hospital handover the pilot who remains flies back to the base: the usual return to base with the base scene (police always after a crew emergency, ambulance only for a crew member aboard at the ambulance limit or below). The end menu comes at the landing on the base. Once per mission (CREW_RTB_STARTED): the 169.29 test showed the report of the handover twice, four minutes apart, and a second call would also start a second return to base.

params.text: Crew handed over to the hospital. Returning to base.

set_message.text: Handover completed. Return to base.

crew hospital unload.#comment: Hospital unload of the critical crew aboard (LifeScore at or below CREW_AMBULANCE_LIMIT, dead or alive), worst first. One stretcher per casualty (chs_str_k). The medic: when one exists (the medic of the patient, ambumedic) it is enough and nothing is created; when none exists (a crew alone, or the patient medic already gone) one medic (chs_med_1) is created at the hospital. He goes to the helicopter with the first stretcher and, with a single casualty, comes back with it; with several he waits there and follows the last stretcher (CHS_TOTAL). With the patient (CHS_PARALLEL yes) the stretchers are already on the scene (crew hospital scene stretchers); this runs in a thread while the patient is handed over and the stretchers leave after the patient. Alone, the stretchers are created here. They follow the hospital waypoints (also the custom ones) to hospital_door and are removed there: arrived, nobody goes anywhere else. Without the ambulance they walk (the next casualty is loaded while the previous one walks), with the ambulance (L:AMBULANCE 1 or 2) it shuttles between the helipad and the door one stretcher at a time. A dead crew member is carried like the others.

set_message.text: Waiting for the ambulance of the patient to be free...
Crew casualties handed over to the hospital.

crew hospital unload 1.#comment: Casualty number 1 of the hospital unload: the member in CCS_LOAD_MEMBER is taken from its seat with its own stretcher (chs_str_1) at its own place (with the patient the stretcher is already on the scene; there is no medic for the crew). The stretcher goes to a point 4 m from the helicopter at the casualty door (around the nose when the door is on the other side than the stretcher, never across the helicopter), the seat is released, the person appears on the stretcher (VAR 2 3), the door closes and the delivery starts (crew hospital deliver walk 1 in its own thread, crew hospital deliver ambulance 1 in sequence). The medic (only the first casualty, when one was created) walks the same route as the stretcher but ends beside the door on the nose side (chs_mdoor_1: 15 degrees toward the nose, 5.5 m, the stretcher comes from abeam to 4 m), so he does not overlap the stretcher, and faces the casualty door.

set_message.text: The hospital team is taking over a crew casualty.

crew hospital deliver walk 1.#comment: The stretcher 1 leaves the helicopter from the casualty door side and follows the hospital waypoints (hospital_wp1..3 when the hospital has them, custom ones included) to hospital_door, where it is removed: arrived, it goes nowhere else. The medic (chs_med_1, only when it was created) follows the last stretcher (CHS_TOTAL 1) the same way, so a single casualty goes back with its stretcher and with several the medic waited at the helicopter. With the patient (CHS_PARALLEL yes) it leaves after the patient has been handed over (L:SAVED 1). When the stretcher has arrived the member is marked as unloaded at the hospital (CREW_HOSPITAL_n 1) and the dispatch page says so.

crew hospital deliver ambulance 1.#comment: With the ambulance: the stretcher 1 goes to the rear of the ambulance (bearing2 180) and is removed there, the ambulance takes the casualty to the hospital door and comes back to its waiting point before the next casualty. The medic (only when it was created) goes to the side of the ambulance with the last stretcher (CHS_TOTAL 1) and is removed when the ambulance is back. With the patient (CHS_PARALLEL yes) the casualties take the ambulance one at a time in order (CHS_AMB_TURN), the first one waiting for the ambulance of the patient to be free. When the stretcher has arrived the member is marked as unloaded at the hospital (CREW_HOSPITAL_n 1) and the dispatch page says so.

set_message.text: Waiting for the ambulance of the patient to be free...
Casualty loaded into the ambulance.

crew hospital unload 2.#comment: Casualty number 2 of the hospital unload: the member in CCS_LOAD_MEMBER is taken from its seat with its own stretcher (chs_str_2) at its own place (with the patient the stretcher is already on the scene; there is no medic for the crew). The stretcher goes to a point 4 m from the helicopter at the casualty door (around the nose when the door is on the other side than the stretcher, never across the helicopter), the seat is released, the person appears on the stretcher (VAR 2 3), the door closes and the delivery starts (crew hospital deliver walk 2 in its own thread, crew hospital deliver ambulance 2 in sequence).

set_message.text: The hospital team is taking over a crew casualty.

crew hospital deliver walk 2.#comment: The stretcher 2 leaves the helicopter from the casualty door side and follows the hospital waypoints (hospital_wp1..3 when the hospital has them, custom ones included) to hospital_door, where it is removed: arrived, it goes nowhere else. The medic (chs_med_1, only when it was created) follows the last stretcher (CHS_TOTAL 2) the same way, so a single casualty goes back with its stretcher and with several the medic waited at the helicopter. With the patient (CHS_PARALLEL yes) it leaves after the patient has been handed over (L:SAVED 1).
